digest_markdown:
Here are 5 bullet points about notable open-source software supply chain attacks or compromises:

* A single compromised maintainer account turned axios, one of the most widely used JavaScript libraries, into a malware delivery system, affecting over 100 million downloads per week. [1]
* Thousands of Node.js developers have unknowingly installed malware via npm packages, with a highly popular package, "rand-user-agent," containing a sophisticated Remote Access Trojan (RAT). [5]
* Hackers compromised Microsoft's official Agent Framework package on PyPI, publishing two malicious versions designed to steal cloud credentials, API keys, and other sensitive developer information. [10]
* Attackers hijacked 10 npm packages to spread PolinRider malware, using the Ethereum blockchain to find a server and download more malware. [6]
* A malicious GitHub Actions workflow, named ".github/workflows/security-audit.yml," was added to hundreds of repositories, stealing credentials from affected repositories and sending them to an external server. [3]
